title: Typing Engine: TypeVar, Generic, Protocol, and get_type_hints

progressiveExplaining.eli5: In standard Python, duck typing means 'if it walks like a duck and quacks like a duck, it is a duck'. `typing.Protocol` is how you describe the duck to your code editor without writing a shared parent class: 'any object that has a `quack()` method is allowed here'.
progressiveExplaining.junior: Python type hints (PEP 484) provide static typing for IDEs and linters (Mypy, Pyright). In modern Python (3.12+), you can define generics using the native syntax `class Stack[T]:` (replacing `TypeVar('T')`). `typing.Protocol` enables **Structural Subtyping** (static duck typing): any class that implements the methods declared in the protocol matches the type without explicit inheritance. `typing.get_type_hints()` allows runtime inspection of annotations.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, Python separates type hinting into **Static Type Analysis** (Mypy/Pyright checking ASTs before execution) and **Runtime Reflection** (Pydantic, FastAPI, and dataclasses inspecting `__annotations__` at runtime). `typing.Protocol` eliminates rigid nominal inheritance, allowing third-party classes to satisfy interfaces without inheriting from shared base classes. In Python 3.12 (PEP 695), generic type parameters are evaluated lazily via the `type` statement: `type Point[T] = tuple[T, T]`.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: When Python evaluates a class with type annotations, it stores them in the class `__annotations__` dictionary (as strings under `from __future__ import annotations` or as raw objects). `typing.get_type_hints(cls)` resolves stringified forward references against the module's global namespace. Protocols use a custom metaclass (`_ProtocolMeta`) that overrides `__subclasscheck__` and `__instancecheck__` using runtime method signature comparison.

codeComparison.title: Nominal Inheritance (ABC) vs Structural Typing (Protocol)
codeComparison.summary: ABCs require rigid class inheritance; `Protocol` allows any class with matching methods to satisfy the type statically.

legacyOrBad.label: Nominal ABC Inheritance
legacyOrBad.snippet: class Renderer(ABC): @abstractmethod def render(self): ... // ❌ Forces explicit subclassing

modernOrGood.label: Structural Protocol Typing (PEP 544)
modernOrGood.snippet: class Renderer(Protocol): def render(self) -> str: ... // ✅ NEW: Static duck typing

interviewGotchas.question: What is the difference between `from __future__ import annotations` (PEP 563) and standard annotations at runtime?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of annotation evaluation performance and runtime reflection.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: Normally, type annotations are evaluated as live Python expressions when the module loads (meaning `x: SomeClass` requires `SomeClass` to already be defined). With `from __future__ import annotations`, **all type annotations are stored as raw strings in `__annotations__` without being evaluated**. This prevents circular import errors and speeds up module load times, but requires runtime libraries (like Pydantic v1) to use `typing.get_type_hints()` to evaluate the strings.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: If using stringified annotations, accessing `obj.__annotations__['x']` directly returns the string `'SomeClass'` instead of the class object; always use `typing.get_type_hints()`.

interviewGotchas.question: How does `typing.runtime_checkable` work with `Protocol`?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks knowledge of runtime `isinstance()` checks on structural protocols.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: By default, Protocols are strictly static (for Mypy/Pyright) and calling `isinstance(obj, MyProtocol)` will raise a `TypeError`. Decorating the protocol with **`@runtime_checkable`** allows `isinstance()` and `issubclass()` to inspect whether the object has the required method/attribute names at runtime.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: `@runtime_checkable` only checks method *existence*, not method *type signatures* or return types at runtime.
